title.narrative: Capacity Building of Local Protection Partners on SGBV Prevention and Response in Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project, led by UNFPA and the GBV Sub-Cluster, aims to enhance the technical and institutional capacity of 20 SHF and local partners, including WLOs. The project will deliver tailored capacity development interventions to Protection and GBV partners, focusing on GBV prevention, response, and risk mitigation.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtWith the proposed funding, UNFPA and selected members of the GBV Area of Responsibility (AoR) will target a diverse range of local actors, including NGOs, CSOs, emergency response responders (ERRs), WLOs, youth-led organizations, SHF Protection partners, and GBV stakeholders under the GBV AoR umbrella.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtDuring the inception phase, a mapping exercise will identify additional local partners, particularly in hard-to-reach areas such as Khartoum, Darfur, and Kordofan. UNFPA aims to engage 400 SHF partner staff from 20 partner organizations through Training of Trainers (ToT), step-down training, mentoring, and coaching sessions over a two-year period. However, the mapping exercise will determine the exact number of staff and provide an updated list of targeted partners for capacity-building activities. Furthermore, a comprehensive needs assessment will inform the planning and design of training topics to ensure they address the specific requirements of participants.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtSpanning two years, the project will empower participants to acquire and apply new skills, thereby enhancing service quality. The extended timeline allows UNFPA and the GBV AoR to oversee the capacity development process, monitor progress, conduct quality checks, and evaluate the project's impact through baseline and endline assessments.ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtThe capacity-building program will offer a comprehensive curriculum, ranging from foundational to advanced topics, including:lt/ligtltligtIASC Minimum Standards for GBV Programming in Humanitarian Settingslt/ligtltligtGBV Case Management with specialized training for individuals with disabilities and male survivorslt/ligtltligtMental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), including Psychological First Aidlt/ligtltligtCare for Child and Adolescent Survivors, focusing on skills to support children affected by GBVlt/ligtltligtManaging GBV in Emergencies, targeting program officers and managerslt/ligtltligtInstitutional development training, including Project and Finance Management, Essentials of Humanitarian Programming, Security, and Negotiation Skills, with a particular emphasis on Jobs of Peace and Access.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtltspangtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtTraining sessions will be delivered in partnership with the International Medical Corps (IMC) through structured workshops and coaching activities. Materials will be drawn from the GBV AoR and Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) guidelines, contextualized to Sudan’s unique needs for sustainability and long-term impact.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtA comprehensive and up-to-date database of GBV/Protection actors participating in the two-year capacity-building program on GBV prevention and response topics will be developed, regularly updated, and maintainedltbrgtlt/pgt
